newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria govt confident about Creditanstalt sale.
newsitem.headline: Austria govt confident about Creditanstalt sale.

text.p: Austrian Finance Minister Viktor Klima said on Monday he had received a host of indicative offers for privatisation candidate Creditanstalt, raising hopes the six-year long sell-off saga might end soon.
"A large number of interested parties has asked for an information memorandum (on the bank)," his office said in a faxed statement. "There were numerous indicative offers."
The confidential study, containing detailed information about the flagship of Austria's overcrowded banking sector, was prepared by J.P. Morgan, the government's advisors in the sale.
The ministry said all bidders, with the exception of an Austro-Italian-German consortium led by insurer EA-Generali, had asked for confidentiality.
"We want to play by the internationally accepted rules," the minister was quoted as saying.

EA-Generali and its co-bidders, including Germany's Commerzbank and Banca Commercialie Italiana, last week said they would submit a bid for the government's 70 percent voting stake in Austria's second-largest bank.
The group reportedly offered around 10 billion schillings ($944.1 million) for a large part of the 19.9 million ordinary shares held by the state. No details about other bids has emerged.

Once the indicative offers had been scrutinised, interested parties would be authorised to take part in the due-diligence process, the ministry said. That stage is expected to last for about two to three weeks.
Final and binding offers would have to be submitted after the close of the due diligence period. "The time for that will be announced in the next few weeks," it said.
"It is stressed once again that a decision on the privatisation will be made this year," the statement said.

Creditanstalt has topped the government's privatisation list since 1991. According to current market prices, the government's stake is worth some 14.5 billion schillings. -- Knut Engelmann, Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274 ($ = 10.59 Austrian Schillings)
